accounting.amortized_from_min: the same table recomputed from each call shape's min sample, as a cross-check on the medians
accounting.amortized_per_repetition_ratio: THE PRIMARY TABLE: for every repetition the ratio unsplit_per_generation / split_per_generation (and / hand_written_per_generation) is computed from that repetition's own samples and the reported number is the median of those --reps ratios; one repetition times every call shape, so a host mode shared by the whole repetition cancels, while two formulations' separate medians can land in different modes (see _meta.shared_host_caveat)
accounting.crossover_reuse_analytic: ceil((split_total_ms + prepare_run - unsplit_total_ms) / (unsplit_run - apply_run)), i.e. the k above which (split_total + prepare_run)/k + apply_run drops below unsplit_total/k + unsplit_run
accounting.crossover_reuse_from_per_repetition_rati: the first N_apply in --reuse whose median per-repetition speedup >= 1.00
accounting.crossover_reuse_measured: the first N_apply in --reuse whose measured speedup >= 1.00
accounting.hand_written_per_generation_ms: (hand_written_total_ms + hand prepare run median) / N_apply + hand apply run median
accounting.run_samples: every raw per-repetition sample of every call shape, in issue order, so the mode mixture behind each table is auditable rather than hidden behind min/median/max
accounting.split_per_generation_ms: (split_total_ms + prepare run median) / N_apply + apply run (median)

_meta.limits: numpy interpreter backend only (host memory on Device('cpu', 0)); no device transfers, no compiled backend and no multi-process measurement are part of this record; the boundary is re-read from host memory, so a device-resident boundary would pay an explicit upload the numpy backend does not model
_meta.note: the top-level _meta describes the most recent run; every runs.<label> entry carries its own date_utc/command/versions/loadavg snapshot so older labels stay self-describing
_meta.protocol: every timed stage is interleaved per repetition (trace, build and run each measure all formulations once per repetition, in the same order) so a contention episode on this shared host is spread across formulations; each call shape gets one untimed warmup
_meta.shared_host_caveat: the host is shared and runs in slow-moving fast/slow modes — the SAME call samples anywhere from ~1.4 to ~59 ms in one 21-repetition cell — so a formulation's min and median are mode statistics, not its cost: all timed stages are interleaved per repetition, the amortized table is reported THREE ways (medians, mins, and the median of per-repetition ratios with the mode cancelled), the load average is recorded at both ends, one timing process runs at a time, and the ratios are the claim while the absolute milliseconds are indicative rather than isolated-hardware measurements

threading.why: this host reports more CPUs to Python than the cgroup actually grants (os.cpu_count vs nproc), so the ambient BLAS/OpenMP pools oversubscribe it and a BLAS-bound cell comes out bimodal, the same work sampling anywhere from a few to tens of milliseconds; the pools are pinned so two formulations are compared on the same footing, and the effective values are recorded here

vmap.reason: the Rust extension evoxc._evoxc_native is not built in this worktree and every builtin transform (vmap included) delegates to it with no Python fallback; the batched comparison is a hand-written graph validated against 64 separate applies
